executive_assessment.text: The SCD reports 87 percent of the population lives in climate hotspots; floods and landslides mainly affect the Kelani basin, including Colombo, which accounts for about 40 percent of GDP.
Estimated average annual disaster fiscal losses exceed US$380 million, of which floods account for about US$240 million.
The implementation plan covers nine adaptation sectors and states that finances, technology, and human capital may constrain delivery of its proposed actions.

geographic_notes.text: Sri Lanka; Kelani River basin; Colombo: The SCD reports 87 percent of the population lives in climate hotspots; floods and landslides mainly affect the Kelani basin, including Colombo, which accounts for about 40 percent of GDP.

Northern Province; North-Central Province; Eastern Province: The SCD reports recent water shortages in Northern, North-Central, and Eastern Provinces; drought also threatens hydropower, which supplies about 30 percent of electricity capacity.

Sri Lanka; Kelani River basin; Colombo; Ambathale: The 2021 program was expected to benefit about 11.2 million people through upgraded weather, flood, and landslide forecasting and early warnings; planned measures include flood-resilient infrastructure in the Kelani basin and a salinity barrier at Ambathale for Colombo's water supply.

known_gaps.text: No inspected Sri Lanka source explicitly links climate hazards to conflict or violence; no climate-FCV pathway is asserted.
The Climate Risk Country Profile and 2025 NDC3 full PDF were inaccessible; claims rely on the opened SCD, government NDC implementation plan, and official World Bank release.
